lines: ¢ Aworker agent never reads this index > it only knows its own folder and the daily log. It doesn't even know the other folders are here. If it needs something outside its lane, you point it there.
- The vault is the brain. Project folders are the hands. Knowledge (anything .md ) lives in here. Code and files live in the project folders on disk.

- Every folder has one note named the exact same thing as the folder. That note is the folder's index. Read it first and it tells you what's in the folder and where to go next. This is the one rule the whole system runs on.
- Memory lives in the vault, never in MEMORY.md . Each agent's MEMORY.md is only a pointer back here. Agents write what they learn into their vault notes, not the auto-memory file Claude ships with.
* One brain, many businesses, many agents. This vault runs two example companies at once. Each has its own folder; they all share the support folders below.
The map (every folder, and who reads it)

* @1 Daily Notes/ : the shared session log. Every agent writes here (## <Agent>: <topic> ), so they all see what the others did.

* 02 Company A/ : the first business: an online info-product company. The customer, the product, the brand, and the jobs its agents run. Start at Company A.   <- the other engine read 'o2 CompanyA/:thefirstbusiness:anonlineinfo-productcompany.Thecustomer,the'
* @3 Company B/ : the second business: a local landscaping company. Same layout as Company A, different notes. Start at Company B.
